(c) Corroboration off-source: Supplement 1's ordering agrees with an independent published PCQ item numbering (Pizzol et al. 2021, Table 3) at 7 of 12 positions including items 1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 11 and 12, while the paper's Table 1 agrees at only 2 of 12 -- Table 1 is the re-ordered listing, not the administered form. note: Clean pass with caveats. (1) The IRW item codes carry no item content: data/KoreanNursing_Park_2017.R runs read.table(header=TRUE) over the Dataverse file 'Jeehp-14-20_raw data.tab', which has NO header row, so the first examinee's 50 zeros and ones became the column names and make.names/make.unique turned them into X0, X1, X1.1, X0.1 ... X0.39. Re-running that line reproduces all 50 live codes in order, so position i = question i; that examinee is absent from the live table, which holds 740 of the study's 741 respondents. (2) resp runs the unusual way round: 1 = INCORRECT, 0 = correct. For all 50 items, (741 - Supplement 7's published number of correct answers) minus that examinee's own score equals the live count of resp==1 EXACTLY (e.g. q1 741-332-0 = 409 = live X0; q13 741-26-1 = 714 = live X1.3). (3) The exam was administered in Korean; neither the article, its seven supplements nor the Dataverse deposit contains a single Hangul character (checked explicitly across suppl1-4, 6, 7), so the fallback applies: the authors' own English from Supplement 7 sits in the base fields, the _translated columns are empty, language=Korean. (4) The five answer options are printed inside item_text after the stem, as Supplement 7 prints them, because resp is a 0/1 score and cannot carry a chosen option; option_text holds the accuracy labels Correct/Incorrect for resp 0/1, which are IRW's words for a direction established from the data, not published labels. (5) No answer key is published; correct_response was derived from Supplement 7's own upper/lower-27% response-distribution tables (the keyed option is the one whose High-27% and Low-27% counts equal the item's High/Low correct counts), unique for 49 of 50 items; item 5's table omits the correct/wrong counts, and its option 3 takes 336/400 = 84% of the extreme groups, matching its published 84% correct-answer rate. (6) Two figures are not reproducible in text: the electronic fetal monitoring graph in case 15 (referenced by q33) and the family health assessment tool / ecomap in case 19 (referenced by q44); q47 refers to 'the underlined information' in case 20's vignette and the underlining is lost in a plain-text transcript. (7) Supplement 7's own numbers are internally inconsistent for q31: it prints 181 correct out of 741 (24.4%) but a correct-answer rate of 27%; the live data agrees with 181.
public_note: Item text for this table is the study authors' English rendering in Supplement 7 of the paper; the mock examination itself was administered in Korean and no Korean wording is published in the article, its supplements or the Harvard Dataverse deposit. Three things about this table are easy to misread: resp runs 1 = INCORRECT and 0 = correct (confirmed item by item against Supplement 7's published correct-answer counts, all 50 exact); the item codes X0, X1, X0.1 ... encode nothing about the items but are R's mangled column names from a headerless raw file whose first examinee was consumed as the header, so the table holds 740 of the study's 741 respondents; and the five answer options appear inside item_text rather than in option_text, which carries the 0/1 accuracy labels instead. The study published no answer key, so correct_response was derived by IRW from Supplement 7's own upper/lower-27% response distributions (unique for 49 of the 50 items; item 5 from its 84% correct-answer rate).

note: MAPPING (paper_order): the IRW item codes ARE the source column names -- data/kraft_todd_2017_empathic_nonverbal.py melts the S3 workbook columns PANASPOS1..10 and PANASNEG1..10 by name (pandas melt, var_name="item"), with no rename and no positional step (core model s3, pattern 1); the live item set is identical to those 20 headers, confirmed server-side with irw_table_sets(). Those headers carry no text, however, so what ties a code to an ADJECTIVE is the S3 column ORDER read against the S2 File's printed item order, and that tie is checked rather than assumed. The workbook orders its PANAS columns PANASPOS1, PANASNEG1, PANASPOS2, PANASNEG2, PANASPOS3, PANASNEG3, PANASNEG4, PANASNEG5, PANASPOS4, PANASPOS5, PANASNEG6, PANASPOS6, PANASNEG7, PANASPOS7, PANASNEG8, PANASPOS8, PANASPOS9, PANASNEG9, PANASPOS10, PANASNEG10 -- valence sequence P N P N P N N N P P N P N P N P P N P N. The S2 File prints Interested, Distressed, Excited, Upset, Strong, Guilty, Scared, Hostile, Enthusiastic, Proud, Irritable, Alert, Ashamed, Inspired, Nervous, Determined, Attentive, Jittery, Active, Afraid, whose published PA/NA keying (PA = positions 1,3,5,9,10,12,14,16,17,19) gives exactly the same sequence: 20/20 positions agree, against a 1/184756 chance under a random 10-of-20 valence assignment. The numbering also ascends strictly with column position within each valence, so the k-th POS column is the k-th positive adjective. CONTENT CORROBORATION, independent of that: all five near-synonym pairs the mapping predicts inside the negative block behave as synonyms in the S3 data -- Scared x Afraid r=0.890 (mutually each other's highest correlate, and the largest r anywhere in the 10x10 negative matrix), Distressed x Upset 0.807 (mutual), Nervous x Jittery 0.747 (Jittery's highest), Hostile x Irritable 0.618 (Hostile's highest), Guilty x Ashamed 0.617 (mutual). Item means are also coherent for a task in which participants watch a doctor deliver bad news: the three attentional PA adjectives top the positive block (Attentive 3.63, Alert 3.44, Interested 3.19) and the three self-conscious/antagonistic NA adjectives sit at the floor (Guilty 1.24, Ashamed 1.26, Hostile 1.40). Route A is what separates the members of each synonym pair (Scared vs Afraid, Alert vs Attentive, Excited vs Enthusiastic); route B corroborates cluster membership. Re-runnable as verify_kraft_todd_2017_panas.R. The S2 File states "all measures were administered via Qualtrics survey software; these are representations of the layout, though the text used was exactly the same". The S3 workbook already stores 1-5 integers and the script does no recoding, so resp is the source's own numeric coding. Direction is corroborated by the floor items: Guilty and Ashamed average 1.24 and 1.26, i.e. sit at "very slightly or not at all", which is what a bad-news vignette should produce.
